meta.title: M365 Graph Cartographer (MGC)
meta.phase: Purview covered in depth from 0.3.0: information protection, records, eDiscovery, audit, privacy and the data security API, with what Graph does not cover.
meta.note: Hand-written content lives here. The scanner never edits this file; it writes graph-map.json alongside it.

workloads.label: Identity & directory
workloads.summary: Entra ID objects: who and what exists in the tenant, and how they are grouped and granted access.
limits: Advanced queries ($count, $search, some $filter on directory objects) need the header ConsistencyLevel: eventual plus $count=true.
Default page size is 100; most directory collections allow $top up to 999.
Use delta queries for sync jobs rather than full re-reads.

workloads.label: Identity governance
workloads.summary: Microsoft Entra ID Governance: access reviews, entitlement management (access packages), lifecycle workflows, Privileged Identity Management, terms of use and admin consent requests.
limits: Licensing moved to Microsoft Entra ID Governance. Features that were generally available in P2 still run on P2; no new governance features are added to P2.
Much of it reads fine with application permissions, but terms of use are delegated only.

workloads.label: Policies
workloads.summary: Tenant-wide Entra policies under /policies and /identity/conditionalAccess: Conditional Access, authentication methods and strengths, cross-tenant access, app and consent policies, and token and sign-in policies.

workloads.label: Mail, calendar & contacts
workloads.summary: Exchange Online mailbox data, reached through a user (or shared mailbox) path.
limits: Outlook throttling: 10,000 requests per 10 minutes and 4 concurrent requests, per app per mailbox.
Application permissions reach every mailbox unless scoped with RBAC for Applications in Exchange Online.
Mailbox must be in Exchange Online (hybrid on-premises mailboxes have extra requirements).

workloads.label: Files & sites
workloads.summary: SharePoint sites, lists and libraries, and OneDrive. Every library is both a list and a drive.
limits: Sites.Selected lets an app reach only the sites you grant it, instead of every site.
Large-list rules still apply: filter on indexed columns to stay under the 5,000-item view threshold.
Much SharePoint admin (hub sites, site scripts, sharing per site) sits outside Graph.

workloads.label: Teams
workloads.summary: Teams, channels, chats and meetings. A team is always backed by a Microsoft 365 group.
limits: Some Teams APIs are metered and have licensing requirements (export and change-notification APIs).
Apps cannot post channel messages with application permissions except in migration mode.
Resource-specific consent (RSC) can scope an app to a single team or chat.

workloads.label: Communications
workloads.summary: Cloud communications under /communications: calls and call records, online meetings with their recordings, transcripts and attendance, and presence.
limits: You may not use the cloud communications APIs to record or otherwise persist media content from calls or meetings that your application accesses (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).

workloads.label: Tasks & planning
workloads.summary: Planner plans and tasks (owned by groups) and personal Microsoft To Do lists.
limits: Planner updates need the If-Match header with the item's current ETag.
Premium plans (Planner Premium / Project) are not exposed through these APIs.

workloads.label: Solutions
workloads.summary: Business solutions under /solutions: Microsoft Bookings, Microsoft 365 Backup, virtual events (webinars and town halls) and cross-tenant migration.

workloads.label: Education
workloads.summary: Education data under /education: schools, classes and education users from School Data Sync, assignments and submissions, and Reflect and Reading Coach reports.

workloads.label: Admin & service health
workloads.summary: Microsoft 365 admin settings under /admin: service health and Message centre, configuration monitoring (baselines and drift), Exchange, SharePoint and Teams admin settings, Microsoft 365 Apps and Edge, and people settings.
limits: Delegated callers of the service communications API need an admin role (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).

workloads.label: Reports & logs
workloads.summary: Usage reports, sign-in logs and directory audit logs.
limits: Entra sign-in and audit logs are kept for 30 days with Entra ID P1/P2 (7 days without). Export to Log Analytics for longer.
Usage reports can conceal user, group and site names unless the tenant report setting is changed.

workloads.label: Security
workloads.summary: Defender XDR alerts and incidents, Secure Score and advanced hunting with KQL.
limits: Use alerts_v2 and incidents. The legacy /security/alerts API is deprecated.
Advanced hunting only sees the last 30 days of Defender data.

workloads.label: Devices (Intune)
workloads.summary: Intune device and app management under /deviceManagement and /deviceAppManagement: managed devices, compliance and configuration policies, apps and app protection, Windows 365 Cloud PCs and endpoint analytics.
limits: The Microsoft Graph API for Intune needs an active Intune licence for the tenant (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).

workloads.label: Compliance & Purview
workloads.summary: Microsoft Purview in Graph: sensitivity labels and classification, records management, eDiscovery (Premium), audit search, subject rights requests and the data security API. Policies themselves (DLP, label, retention, IRM) are mostly outside Graph.
limits: Policies (DLP, label publishing, auto-labelling, retention, Information Barriers, Insider Risk) are not in Graph. See Not in Graph: Purview.
Several Purview APIs are delegated only (retention labels, subject rights requests). Check the application permission on each node.
Learn and $metadata sometimes disagree on beta versus v1.0 (for example eDiscovery legal holds). The scan badge shows what $metadata says today.

workloads.label: AI & agents
workloads.summary: Copilot interaction history and Entra Agent ID (agent identities and their blueprints). Your own AI apps apply Purview policy through the Purview data security API, which sits in the Purview workload.
limits: Most of these APIs are new. Licensing and preview status drift, so check the date each note was verified.
Copilot Studio agents are not covered by the Copilot interaction export.

hub.label: Microsoft Graph
hub.summary: One REST endpoint over Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Windows and EMS data. Every node on this map hangs off it.

permissions.delegated: Acts as the signed-in user: effective access is the overlap of the app's scopes and the user's own rights.
permissions.application: Acts as the app itself, with no user. Needs admin consent and usually reaches the whole tenant.

limits: Throttled requests return 429 with a Retry-After header. Back off and retry.
JSON batching ($batch) allows up to 20 requests per batch.
Collections are paged. Always follow @odata.nextLink.
beta can change without notice and is not supported for production.
mapping: Read $metadata to see every entity type and relationship: https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/$metadata
Prefer delta queries and change notifications over polling.

nodes.label: User
nodes.summary: A person (member or guest) in Entra ID. The anchor for most personal data in Microsoft 365.
nodes.licence: Directory reads need no add-on licence. signInActivity needs Entra ID P1/P2.
limits: Only a default set of properties comes back. Use $select for the rest.
signInActivity needs AuditLog.Read.All as well.
$search and many $filter queries need ConsistencyLevel: eventual.
mapping: /users/{id}/drive goes to their OneDrive.
/users/{id}/messages, /events and /contacts go to their mailbox.
/users/{id}/memberOf lists groups and roles (use transitiveMemberOf for nested groups).

nodes.label: Group
nodes.summary: Microsoft 365 groups, security groups, mail-enabled security groups and distribution lists.
nodes.licence: Dynamic membership needs Entra ID P1.
limits: Graph can only create Microsoft 365 groups and security groups. Distribution lists and mail-enabled security groups are read-only here (use Exchange PowerShell).
Conversations, calendar and Planner exist only on Microsoft 365 groups.
groupTypes contains 'Unified' for Microsoft 365 groups.
mapping: /groups/{id}/drive and /sites/root go to the connected SharePoint site.
/groups/{id}/team gives the team, if the group is team-enabled.
/groups/{id}/members lists direct members (use transitiveMembers for nested).

nodes.label: Application
nodes.summary: An app registration: the global definition of an app, held in its home tenant.
nodes.licence: None.
limits: Secret values can only be read once, at creation.
Only exists in the app's home tenant. Other tenants see only its service principal.
mapping: Joined to its service principal by appId, not by a navigation property.
requiredResourceAccess lists the permissions the app asks for, not what has been granted.

nodes.label: Service principal
nodes.summary: An enterprise app: the app's identity in this tenant. Grants and assignments are recorded here.
nodes.licence: None.
limits: Granted application permissions are listed under appRoleAssignments. Delegated grants are under oauth2PermissionGrants.
Managed identities are service principals too (servicePrincipalType = ManagedIdentity).
mapping: Microsoft Graph itself is the service principal with appId 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000. Its appRoles and oauth2PermissionScopes list every Graph permission.
/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignedTo shows who has been assigned the app.

nodes.label: Device
nodes.summary: A device registered or joined in Entra ID.
nodes.licence: None for Entra device objects. Intune data needs Intune licences.
limits: This is the Entra device object, not the Intune record. Intune devices are under /deviceManagement/managedDevices (DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All).
Match the two using deviceId (Entra) and azureADDeviceId (Intune).
mapping: /users/{id}/registeredDevices and /ownedDevices link users to devices.

nodes.label: Administrative unit
nodes.summary: A container that scopes admin roles to a subset of users, groups or devices.
nodes.licence: Entra ID P1 for administrators assigned to an administrative unit.
limits: Restricted management administrative units block even tenant-wide admins from changing members.
mapping: /directory/administrativeUnits/{id}/members.
Scoped role assignments are under /directory/administrativeUnits/{id}/scopedRoleMembers.

nodes.label: Directory role
nodes.summary: Entra admin roles such as Global Administrator and Compliance Administrator.
nodes.licence: PIM (eligible assignments) needs Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance.
limits: /directoryRoles lists only roles that have been activated in the tenant.
/directoryRoles/{id}/members misses PIM-eligible users. Use roleEligibilitySchedules for those.
mapping: Prefer /roleManagement/directory (unifiedRoleDefinition, roleAssignments) for complete answers.

nodes.label: Message
nodes.summary: An email in a mailbox folder.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: $search and $filter cannot be combined on messages.
Attachments of 3 to 150 MB need an upload session. Default message size limit is 35 MB.
Shared mailboxes are read through /users/{shared-mailbox}/messages (Mail.Read.Shared when delegated).
mapping: Use mailFolders/{wellKnownName}/messages, for example inbox or sentitems.
Sensitivity label metadata appears in internet headers, not as a first-class property.

nodes.label: Mail folder
nodes.summary: A folder in a mailbox. Folders can be nested.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: Only the top level is returned by default. Walk childFolders, or use includeHiddenFolders=true for hidden ones.
Archive mailbox folders sit under the well-known name 'archive'.
mapping: Well-known names: inbox, drafts, sentitems, deleteditems, archive, junkemail.

nodes.label: Event
nodes.summary: A calendar appointment or meeting.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: /events returns recurring series masters. Use /calendarView to expand individual occurrences.
Times are UTC unless you send the header Prefer: outlook.timezone="GMT Standard Time".
mapping: Teams meeting details are in onlineMeeting.joinUrl. Use it to look up the onlineMeeting object.

nodes.label: Calendar
nodes.summary: A calendar container: the user's default calendar, extra calendars, or a group calendar.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: Shared calendars can be read only where the mailbox owner has shared them, or with application permissions.
mapping: /users/{id}/calendar is the default calendar.
Free/busy across people: POST /users/{id}/calendar/getSchedule.

nodes.label: Contact
nodes.summary: A personal contact in the user's mailbox.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: Personal contacts only. This is not the global address list.
mapping: For the directory use /users. For relevance-ranked people use /me/people (People.Read).

nodes.label: Site
nodes.summary: A SharePoint site: team site, communication site, or a OneDrive's underlying site.
nodes.licence: SharePoint Online.
limits: Sites.Selected needs a second step: grant the app access with POST /sites/{id}/permissions.
Hub association, site scripts and many site-level admin settings need SharePoint REST, PnP or SPO PowerShell.
/sites?search= relies on the search index, so new sites can be missing for a while.
mapping: A site ID is a composite: hostname,siteCollectionId,webId.
Tenant-wide sharing settings: /admin/sharepoint/settings (SharePointTenantSettings.Read.All).

nodes.label: List
nodes.summary: A SharePoint list or library. Columns and content types live here.
nodes.licence: SharePoint Online.
limits: Filtering on a non-indexed column fails on large lists. The Prefer: HonorNonIndexedQueriesWarningMayFailRandomly header is a workaround with no guarantees.
Some column types (for example managed metadata) come back with limited detail.
mapping: A document library has /lists/{id}/drive. That is the same container seen as files.

nodes.label: List item
nodes.summary: A row in a list. In a library, each file is also a list item that carries its metadata.
nodes.licence: SharePoint Online.
limits: Column values only come back with $expand=fields (use $select inside it).
Item-level permissions are not exposed on listItem. Go through the driveItem for files.
mapping: /items/{id}/driveItem goes to the file, and /driveItem/listItem comes back.

nodes.label: Drive
nodes.summary: A document library or a OneDrive.
nodes.licence: SharePoint Online or OneDrive.
limits: quota shows storage used and remaining, which is useful for storage-reduction work.
Delta (/root/delta) is the reliable way to enumerate or sync a large library.
mapping: /drives/{id}/root/children lists the top level.
/drives/{id}/list goes to the matching SharePoint list.

nodes.label: Drive item
nodes.summary: A file or folder.
nodes.licence: SharePoint Online or OneDrive. assignSensitivityLabel is a metered API.
limits: Simple PUT upload handles up to 250 MB. Larger files need an upload session (fragments under 60 MiB, in multiples of 320 KiB).
App-only calls cannot replace the content of a file protected by a sensitivity label. Use delegated permissions.
assignSensitivityLabel needs metered API billing set up on an Azure subscription.
mapping: /permissions shows sharing links and grants.
/retentionLabel reads or sets the retention label.
/versions shows version history, which counts towards storage.

nodes.label: Sharing permission
nodes.summary: A sharing link or direct grant on a file, folder or site. On sites, lists and list items, Graph can only create permissions for applications (the Selected scopes model), not for users.

permissions.delegated: Files.Read.All (files). Sites.Read.All for site, list and list item permissions
permissions.application: Files.Read.All or Sites.Selected (files). Sites.Read.All for site, list and list item permissions

nodes.licence: SharePoint Online or OneDrive.
limits: Inherited entries show inheritedFrom. SharePoint group membership is not expanded.
'Limited access' entries are not shown.
For tenant-wide oversharing reviews, SharePoint Advanced Management or DSPM reports are often quicker than walking every item.
mapping: The link property gives the scope (anonymous, organisation, users) and the type (view, edit).

nodes.label: Not in Graph: SharePoint
nodes.path: SharePoint REST · PnP PowerShell · SPO Management Shell
nodes.summary: SharePoint administration that Graph doesn't fully cover yet.
limits: Hub site registration and association.
Site designs and site scripts.
Per-site sharing capability and many site-level settings.
Container (site) sensitivity label assignment for non-group sites.
mapping: Check the beta scan results on Site. Coverage moves over time.

nodes.label: Team
nodes.summary: Teams settings layered on top of a Microsoft 365 group. The team and the group share the same ID.
nodes.licence: Teams.
limits: POST /teams is asynchronous. It returns 202 with an operation to poll.
Archived teams are read-only.
mapping: /teams/{id}/group goes back to the group. Membership is managed on the group.
/users/{id}/joinedTeams lists a user's teams.

nodes.label: Channel
nodes.summary: A standard, private or shared channel in a team.
nodes.licence: Teams.
limits: Private and shared channels have their own SharePoint site, separate from the team's site.
Shared channels can include people from other tenants (B2B direct connect).
mapping: /filesFolder gives the channel's folder as a driveItem.
membershipType is standard, private or shared.

nodes.label: Chat
nodes.summary: A one-to-one, group or meeting chat.
nodes.licence: Teams.
limits: Tenant-wide chat export (/users/{id}/chats/getAllMessages) is metered and needs the appropriate licences.
mapping: chatType is oneOnOne, group or meeting.
Meeting chats are linked to the onlineMeeting by its chatInfo threadId.

nodes.label: Chat message
nodes.summary: A post or reply in a channel, or a message in a chat.
nodes.licence: Teams. Export and notification APIs are metered.
limits: Apps cannot send channel messages with application permissions, except for migration (Teamwork.Migrate.All).
Replies are fetched separately: /messages/{id}/replies.
Files attached in messages live in SharePoint or OneDrive, not in Teams.
mapping: Attachments point to driveItems by URL.

nodes.label: Online meeting
nodes.summary: A Teams meeting, with its transcripts, recordings and attendance reports.
nodes.licence: Teams.
limits: App-only access needs a Teams application access policy (New-CsApplicationAccessPolicy) as well as the Graph permission. Policy changes take up to 30 minutes to apply.
Usually found by joinWebUrl from the calendar event. There is no simple list of all meetings.
mapping: /transcripts and /recordings are under the meeting (OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All, OnlineMeetingRecording.Read.All).

nodes.label: Planner plan
nodes.summary: A basic Planner plan, contained by a Microsoft 365 group.
nodes.licence: Planner (basic).
limits: Updates need If-Match with the current ETag.
Premium plans are not available here.
mapping: container (or owner) points to the group.
/buckets and /tasks hang off the plan.

nodes.label: Planner task
nodes.summary: A card in a plan.
nodes.licence: Planner (basic).
limits: Description and checklist are in a separate resource: /tasks/{id}/details.
mapping: assignments are keyed by user ID.

nodes.label: To Do list
nodes.summary: A personal Microsoft To Do list, stored in the user's mailbox.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: Personal to one user. Planner tasks assigned to the user appear in To Do but come from Planner.
mapping: /me/todo/lists/{id}/tasks.

nodes.label: To Do task
nodes.summary: A task in a To Do list.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: linkedResources can point to the source item, such as a flagged email.
mapping: Supports delta for sync.

nodes.label: Usage reports
nodes.summary: Microsoft 365 usage reports for Teams, Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Copilot and more.
nodes.licence: Included. The caller also needs a reports reader role when delegated.
limits: Many reports return a CSV via redirect rather than JSON.
Names are concealed by default. The tenant setting is at /admin/reportSettings.
Data lags by roughly two days. Periods are D7, D30, D90 and D180.
mapping: SharePoint and OneDrive storage per site: getSharePointSiteUsageDetail.

nodes.label: Sign-in log
nodes.summary: Entra ID sign-in events.
nodes.licence: Entra ID P1/P2.
limits: v1.0 returns interactive sign-ins only. beta adds non-interactive, service principal and managed identity sign-ins via signInEventTypes.
Kept for 30 days. Send to Log Analytics or Sentinel for longer.
mapping: userId and appId link to the user and the service principal.

nodes.label: Directory audit
nodes.summary: Entra ID change history: who changed what in the directory.
nodes.licence: Entra ID free (7 days) or P1/P2 (30 days).
limits: Entra changes only. Microsoft 365 workload activity is in the Purview unified audit log (see Audit log query).
mapping: targetResources and initiatedBy reference users, groups and apps by ID.

nodes.label: Alert (v2)
nodes.summary: A Defender XDR alert from any Defender product, including Purview DLP and Insider Risk alerts.
nodes.licence: Matching Defender or Purview product.
limits: Don't build on the legacy /security/alerts. It is deprecated.
mapping: incidentId links to the incident.
evidence lists the users, devices, files and mailboxes involved.

nodes.label: Incident
nodes.summary: A group of related alerts, correlated by Defender XDR.
nodes.licence: Defender XDR.
limits: $expand=alerts is the efficient way to get the alerts with the incident.
mapping: /incidents/{id}/alerts.

nodes.label: Secure Score
nodes.summary: A daily snapshot of the tenant's Microsoft Secure Score.
nodes.licence: Included.
limits: One snapshot per day. Improvement actions are in /security/secureScoreControlProfiles.
mapping: controlScores breaks the score down by control.

nodes.label: Advanced hunting
nodes.summary: Runs a KQL query over Defender XDR advanced hunting tables, for example CloudAppEvents for AI app usage.
nodes.licence: Defender XDR.
limits: Only the last 30 days of data.
Up to 100,000 rows and 50 MB per result.
At least 45 calls per minute per tenant. Requests over three minutes time out. A 429 means the CPU quota is used up.
mapping: An action, not an entity: send { "Query": "..." }.

nodes.label: Sensitivity label
nodes.summary: Read the published sensitivity labels. Apply them to files through driveItem actions.

permissions.delegated: SensitivityLabel.Read (higher: SensitivityLabels.Read.All). Beta informationProtection path: InformationProtectionPolicy.Read
permissions.application: SensitivityLabel.Read (higher: SensitivityLabels.Read.All). Beta informationProtection path: InformationProtectionPolicy.Read.All

nodes.licence: Purview Information Protection.
limits: Read-only. Label creation and label policies need Security & Compliance PowerShell.
v1.0 exposes labels through the data security and governance API. The informationProtection path is beta.
mapping: Apply to a file: POST /drives/{id}/items/{id}/assignSensitivityLabel (metered).
Read from a file: extractSensitivityLabels.

Effective rights and label inheritance: POST /security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/sensitivityLabels/computeRightsAndInheritance (v1.0, SensitivityLabel.Evaluate). Returns the content rights, the inherited label and the labels for each item.

legacy.note: Deprecated beta API. Learn says it stopped returning data on 1 January 2023, and its evaluate and extract actions are deprecated too.

nodes.label: Retention label
nodes.summary: Records management retention labels: retention period and trigger, what happens at the end (including disposition review), file plan descriptors and the event type for event-based retention.
nodes.licence: Basic retention labels: Microsoft 365 E3. Event-based retention and disposition review: Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E5/A5/G5, Purview Suite, or E5 Information Protection and Governance (Purview service description, checked 16 Nov 2026).
limits: Delegated only: listing and creating retention labels has no application permission.
Label policies (publishing and auto-apply) are not in Graph. Use Security & Compliance PowerShell.
A label's event type can't be changed once the label is saved.
mapping: Applied on files through /drives/{id}/items/{id}/retentionLabel (matched by label name, not ID).
retentionTrigger dateOfEvent plus retentionEventType makes it event-based; descriptors carry the file plan; dispositionReviewStages set the reviewers.

nodes.label: eDiscovery case
nodes.summary: Purview eDiscovery cases: custodians, non-custodial sources, searches, holds, review sets and exports.
nodes.licence: Microsoft 365 E3: delegated calls for cases, custodians, searches and holds (export needs pay-as-you-go). E5 or an equivalent add-on: app-only calls and premium features such as review sets, tagging and analytics.
limits: Searches, holds and exports are long-running operations to poll.
Delegated callers also need a Purview role: eDiscovery Manager (own cases) or eDiscovery Administrator.
Not for journaling or mass download of content.
mapping: Custodians reference users (mailbox and OneDrive), sites and Microsoft 365 groups.

legacy.note: Deprecated beta API. Learn gives no retirement date.

nodes.label: Audit log query
nodes.summary: Searches the Purview unified audit log asynchronously.
nodes.licence: Purview Audit (Standard): 180 days. Audit (Premium): 1 year by default for Entra, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint records of E5-licensed users, up to 10 years with the add-on.
limits: Asynchronous: create the query, poll its status, then page through /records.
Permissions are split per workload. Pick the narrowest one.
recordTypeFilters take PascalCase values, for example CopilotInteraction or ComplianceDLPSharePoint.
mapping: records holds the audit records (see Audit record); auditData carries the workload-specific payload.

nodes.label: Not in Graph: Purview
nodes.path: Security & Compliance PowerShell (Connect-IPPSSession) · Purview portal · Purview REST APIs
nodes.summary: Purview solutions and configuration that Graph does not expose, with what to use instead.
limits: DLP policies and rules: Get-DlpCompliancePolicy and Get-DlpComplianceRule. DLP alerts are in Graph (alerts_v2).
Sensitivity labels and label policies: Get-Label and Get-LabelPolicy. Labels can be read in Graph; their policies can't.
Auto-labelling policies: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy.
Retention policies: Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy. Only retention labels are in Graph.
Information Barriers: Get-InformationBarrierPolicy, Get-OrganizationSegment and Start-InformationBarrierPoliciesApplication.
Communication Compliance: Get-SupervisoryReviewPolicyV2, and the Purview portal for reviews.

Insider Risk Management: no policy API. Alerts reach alerts_v2 and incidents once IRM shares data with Defender, and activity can be hunted with runHuntingQuery. The only Graph hook is the beta insiderRiskyUserApproval for access packages.
DSPM and DSPM for AI: Purview portal only.
Compliance Manager: Purview portal only.
Data Map and Unified Catalog: separate Purview REST APIs, not Graph. Learn says they are moving into Microsoft Fabric, with existing capabilities in maintenance until 12 Nov 2027.
mapping: Plan automation on Security & Compliance PowerShell for policies. The scanner watches $metadata and flags new Purview types.

legacy.note: In beta $metadata but not documented on Learn.
legacy.replacedBy: Purview data security API (processContent) for runtime checks; Get-DlpCompliancePolicy to read policies

nodes.label: Conditional Access policy
nodes.summary: The tenant's Conditional Access policies: who and what they target, the conditions, and the grant and session controls.
nodes.licence: Entra ID P1. Policies that target agents need Microsoft Agent 365 (included in Microsoft 365 E7) plus Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 E3 (checked 16 Nov 2026).
limits: Policies that target all users do not include agent users. Target agents explicitly (all agent identities, selected agents, or by blueprint; preview).
Agent policies apply only when the agent uses its own identity, not when it acts on behalf of a user.
Conditional Access is not enforced when a blueprint gets a token to create agent identities.
mapping: conditions.users and conditions.clientApplications hold the user, group, role, workload identity and agent targets by ID.
Each sign-in records the policies that applied in appliedConditionalAccessPolicies.

nodes.label: Risky user
nodes.summary: Users that Entra ID Protection flags as at risk, with risk level, state and history. Admins can confirm compromise or dismiss risk.
nodes.licence: Entra ID P2 for full data and the confirmCompromised and dismiss actions. P1 and Free see only medium and high risk users, with no history.
limits: confirmCompromised (sets risk to high) and dismiss (sets it to none) need IdentityRiskyUser.ReadWrite.All and at least Security Administrator.
$top is capped at 500.
mapping: The risky user id is the user's object ID, so it joins straight to /users/{id} and to sign-in userId.

nodes.label: OAuth grant
nodes.summary: Delegated permission grants: which client app may call which API on behalf of one user or all users, and with which scopes.
nodes.licence: None beyond Entra ID.
limits: /users/{id}/oauth2PermissionGrants returns only that user's own grants, not admin-consented AllPrincipals grants, and does not support application permissions.
Expect replication delays. Filter on clientId to reduce them.
mapping: clientId is the object ID of the client service principal; resourceId is the API's service principal (for example Microsoft Graph).
consentType AllPrincipals means admin consent for everyone; Principal means one user consented.

nodes.label: App role assignment
nodes.summary: Who holds an app role on an application: users and groups assigned to enterprise apps, and application permissions granted to other apps.
nodes.licence: None beyond Entra ID. Group assignment to apps needs Entra ID P1.
limits: The per-user list also returns assignments to groups the user is a direct member of.
Learn lists AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All as the least delegated permission for the per-user list. It also lets an app grant itself more privilege, so prefer Directory.Read.All for read-only tools.
Expect replication delays. Use ConsistencyLevel: eventual with $count for complete counts.
mapping: principalId is the user, group or service principal; resourceId is the service principal that owns the role; appRoleId is the role.
Application permissions granted to an app (for example Mail.Read on Graph) are app role assignments too.

nodes.label: PIM eligibility
nodes.summary: Privileged Identity Management eligible assignments: who can activate a directory role, for which scope and until when.
nodes.licence: Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance, for eligible users, approvers and reviewers.
limits: Active (permanent or activated) roles are in roleAssignmentSchedules, not here. Review both.
If the licence lapses, eligible assignments are removed and activation through the API stops.
mapping: principalId is the user or group; roleDefinitionId matches the directory role's roleTemplateId; directoryScopeId is / or an administrative unit.

nodes.label: Licence
nodes.summary: The tenant's licence SKUs with purchased and consumed units and service plans. Per user, licenseDetails shows what each user holds.
nodes.licence: None.
limits: GET /users/{id}/licenseDetails lists no application permission on Learn. App-only tools can read assignedLicenses on the user (User.Read.All) instead.
Group-based licensing errors are written to the user asynchronously, not when the licence is assigned.
mapping: Join on skuId: user.assignedLicenses, group.assignedLicenses and licenseDetails all carry it.
user.licenseAssignmentStates shows whether each licence is direct or inherited from a group.

nodes.label: Inbox rule
nodes.summary: A user's Inbox rules, including forwardTo, redirectTo and forwardAsAttachmentTo actions that send mail outside the organisation.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online mailbox.
limits: Only Inbox rules are exposed. Mailbox-level forwarding and transport rules are not in Graph.
Forwarding is blocked if the remote domain or the outbound spam policy disables automatic forwarding, so a rule can exist and still not forward.
Forward and redirect rules allow at most 10 recipients.
mapping: Check actions.forwardTo, redirectTo and forwardAsAttachmentTo for addresses outside your accepted domains.

nodes.label: Not in Graph: Exchange
nodes.summary: Exchange forwarding and mail flow controls that Graph does not expose.
limits: Mailbox-level forwarding: Get-Mailbox (ForwardingAddress, ForwardingSmtpAddress, DeliverToMailboxAndForward) and Set-Mailbox.
Outbound spam policy: Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy, AutoForwardingMode (Automatic, On, Off). Set it explicitly; Automatic now behaves as Off for most tenants.
Remote domains: Get-RemoteDomain, AutoForwardEnabled.
Mail flow (transport) rules: Get-TransportRule.
mapping: When one control allows forwarding and another blocks it, the block usually wins.
Remote domain settings don't affect admin-set mailbox forwarding or forwarding by transport rules.

nodes.label: Copilot interaction
nodes.summary: A user's Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses across Teams, Word, Outlook and other apps, with the files and links Copilot used.
nodes.licence: Microsoft 365 Copilot licence (service plan Microsoft Copilot with Graph-grounded chat) for the user.
limits: Does not return interactions with Copilot Studio agents.
No delta. A createdDateTime filter needs both a lower and an upper bound; filter on appClass to pick one app.
Application permission only, so the app can read every licensed user's history. Treat the consent as highly sensitive.
mapping: contexts and attachments hold the URLs and IDs of the files, mails and messages Copilot used.
requestId and sessionId pair a prompt with its response.

nodes.label: Purview data security API
nodes.summary: Lets any app (AI, line-of-business or SaaS) apply Purview policy: compute which DLP and label policies apply, send content for a verdict, or just log the activity for audit.
nodes.licence: Pay-as-you-go billing must be enabled for Entra-registered AI apps (charged per request for non-Microsoft 365 AI). Checked 16 Nov 2026.
limits: Cache the ETag from compute and send it as If-None-Match on processContent. Call compute again when protectionScopeState is modified.
DLP policies for Entra-registered apps must be created with New-DlpComplianceRule. Policies made in the portal UI don't apply to them.
evaluateInline makes the app wait for the verdict; evaluateOffline does not.
Higher permissions are ProtectionScopes.Compute.All and Content.Process.All.
mapping: compute: which users, apps and activities (uploadText, downloadText, uploadFile, downloadFile) are in scope. processContent: the verdict and policy actions (such as block). contentActivities: audit only.
A tenant-wide compute is at /security/dataSecurityAndGovernance/protectionScopes/compute.
Microsoft 365 Copilot is covered by Purview natively; this API is for your own apps and agents.

nodes.label: Agent identity
nodes.summary: An Entra Agent ID identity: a service principal subtype that an AI agent signs in with, created from an agent identity blueprint.
nodes.licence: Agent ID is available to Entra customers; Conditional Access, ID Protection and Governance for agents need Microsoft Agent 365 (in Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on). Learn pages disagree, so treat as drifting (checked 16 Nov 2026).
limits: High-risk Graph permissions (such as Application.ReadWrite.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.All, User.ReadWrite.All) cannot be granted to agents.
The admin consent workflow does not work for agent identities.
The blueprint's owner can manage every agent identity created from it without a directory role.
mapping: agentIdentityBlueprintId links to the blueprint. As a service principal it has app role assignments and OAuth grants like any other app.
Agent sign-ins appear in the sign-in log; the agent property that marks them is beta only.

nodes.label: Agent blueprint
nodes.summary: An agent identity blueprint: an application subtype that defines a kind of agent and creates its agent identities.
nodes.licence: As for agent identity (drifting; checked 16 Nov 2026).
limits: GET /applications also returns blueprints; tell them apart by @odata.type.
Audit logs record blueprint operations under ApplicationManagement and do not mark them as agents by default.
mapping: A Conditional Access policy that targets a blueprint covers every agent identity created from it, including later ones.

nodes.label: Sensitive info type
nodes.summary: Built-in and custom sensitive information types (SITs) that DLP and auto-labelling use to find data such as card numbers.
nodes.licence: Custom and EDM-based SITs need E5-class Information Protection.
limits: Beta only, and Learn documents the resource but no methods. Don't build production tooling on it.
Get-DlpSensitiveInformationType in Security & Compliance PowerShell is the documented way to list SITs.
mapping: sensitiveTypeSource tells built-in (outOfBox) from custom (tenant) types; classificationMethod tells pattern, EDM and trainable types apart.

nodes.label: EDM data store
nodes.summary: Exact data match (EDM) stores: the hashed table of real values (for example customer numbers) that EDM-based SITs match against.
nodes.licence: E5-class Information Protection.
limits: Beta only and not documented on Learn. Uploads go through sessions (commit) and registered upload agents.
The supported route is the EDM Upload Agent (EdmUploadAgent.exe); the uploader must be in the EDM_DataUploaders group.
mapping: An EDM store backs one or more EDM-based sensitive info types.

nodes.label: Retention event
nodes.summary: Starts the retention period for content labelled with an event-based label, such as an employee leaving or a contract ending. Event types are the catalogue of such events.
nodes.licence: Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E5/A5/G5, Purview Suite, or E5 Information Protection and Governance (Purview service description, checked 16 Nov 2026).
limits: eventQueries match SharePoint and OneDrive content by asset ID (for example AssetID:1234) and Exchange by keywords.
Content needs the asset ID (the Compliance Asset Id column) before the event fires, or it won't be matched.
Creating events needs RecordsManagement.ReadWrite.All.
mapping: A retention label with retentionTrigger dateOfEvent is bound to one event type; an event of that type starts the clock.

nodes.label: File plan descriptor
nodes.summary: File plan metadata on a retention label: authority, category and subcategory, citation, department and file plan reference.

permissions.application: RecordsManagement.Read.All (template lists; descriptors on a label are delegated only)

nodes.licence: Purview Records Management (file plan).
limits: The descriptor has no methods of its own: read it by expanding descriptors on the retention label.
Templates are bound to a label with descriptors.{x}Template@odata.bind.
mapping: Subcategories sit under categories (/security/labels/categories/{id}/subcategories).

nodes.label: Disposition review
nodes.path: dispositionReviewStages[] on POST or PATCH /security/labels/retentionLabels (no path of its own)
nodes.summary: Up to five review stages, each with named reviewers, that must approve before labelled content is deleted at the end of its retention period.

permissions.delegated: RecordsManagement.ReadWrite.All (to set stages on a label)

nodes.licence: Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E5/A5/G5, Purview Suite, or E5 Information Protection and Governance (Purview service description, checked 16 Nov 2026).
limits: Graph sets the stages on the label; the reviews themselves happen in the Purview portal.
Reviewers need the Disposition Management role, which Global Administrators don't get by default.
Auditing must be turned on for disposition to work.
mapping: Set actionAfterRetentionPeriod to startDispositionReview on the label.

nodes.label: Custodian
nodes.summary: A person of interest in an eDiscovery case, with their data sources: mailbox and OneDrive, sites and Microsoft 365 groups.
nodes.licence: As for eDiscovery case (E3 delegated; E5 for app-only).
limits: Adding sources, holds and release are writes: eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All.
Indexing of custodian sources is asynchronous (lastIndexOperation).
mapping: userSources point at the user's mailbox and OneDrive by email; siteSources and unifiedGroupSources at sites and groups.

nodes.label: eDiscovery search
nodes.summary: A KQL search over custodian and non-custodial sources, with statistics estimates before you collect anything.
nodes.licence: As for eDiscovery case.
limits: estimateStatistics is asynchronous; poll lastEstimateStatisticsOperation.
mapping: custodianSources and noncustodialSources say what is searched; addToReviewSetOperation tracks collection.

nodes.label: Review set
nodes.summary: Collected copies of search results for review, tagging and export.
nodes.licence: E5 or an equivalent eDiscovery add-on (premium feature).
limits: addToReviewSet and export are asynchronous operations.
Learn documents export with eDiscovery.Read.All as the least privilege.
mapping: queries are saved review set filters; export writes to a storage location you choose.

nodes.label: Legal hold
nodes.summary: Preserves a custodian's or a non-custodial source's content in place so it can't be permanently deleted while the case is open.

permissions.delegated: eDiscovery.Read.All (Learn lists it even for applyHold)

nodes.licence: As for eDiscovery case.
limits: applyHold and removeHold on custodians and non-custodial sources are v1.0 in $metadata, and run as ediscoveryHoldOperation.
The hold policy resource (legalHolds, ediscoveryHoldPolicy) is beta only in $metadata, although Learn documents it under v1.0 (checked 16 Nov 2026).
Holds take time to apply; check the operation before relying on them.
mapping: Put the hold on before the account is disabled, the licence removed or the OneDrive deleted.

nodes.label: Audit record
nodes.summary: One unified audit log event from an audit log query: who did what, to which object, when and from where.
nodes.licence: Audit (Standard): 180 days. Audit (Premium): 1 year by default for E5 users, up to 10 years with the add-on.
limits: auditData is a typed payload per record type. DLP audit types are partly beta (a security.dlp namespace in beta $metadata, which Learn doesn't document) and partly v1.0 (dlpImportResultAuditRecord, powerBIDlpAuditRecord).
Higher permissions are per workload: -Exchange, -SharePoint, -OneDrive, -Endpoint, -CRM, then AuditLogsQuery.Read.All.
mapping: userPrincipalName and userId identify the actor; objectId is often the file URL or message ID.

nodes.label: Subject rights request
nodes.summary: Priva subject rights requests (access, deletion, export) for a data subject, with notes, approvers, collaborators and the final report.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Priva Subject Rights Requests (licence not re-checked on 16 Nov 2026).
limits: Delegated only.
The data subject is usually not a user in your tenant; it's described by name and email in dataSubject.
mapping: getFinalReport and getFinalAttachment return the outputs once the request completes.
team is the Microsoft Teams team created for collaborating on the request.

legacy.note: Learn says this path stopped returning data on 30 March 2025.

nodes.label: Message trace
nodes.summary: Exchange Online message trace: where each message went, its status, and per-recipient delivery events.
nodes.licence: Exchange Online.
limits: Provision the Exchange message trace service principal first (appId 8bd644d1-64a1-4d4b-ae52-2e0cbf64e373, New-MgServicePrincipal).
100 requests per 5 minutes per tenant.
90 days of data, at most 10 days per query (filter receivedDateTime with both bounds); with no filter, the last 48 hours.
mapping: messageId is the internet message ID; senderAddress and recipientAddress match users by email.
Per-recipient events: /messageTraces/{id}/getDetailsByRecipient(recipientAddress='...').

nodes.label: Access review
nodes.summary: Access review definitions and their recurring instances: who reviews which groups, apps, access packages or roles, and when.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID Governance (capabilities that were generally available in P2 still run on P2). Reviews of inactive users only, machine-learning recommendations and catalog reviews need ID Governance.
limits: Default page size is 100; page with $top and $skip to avoid timeouts.
Filter definitions by scope with contains(scope/microsoft.graph.accessReviewQueryScope/query,'/groups'); this doesn't work on inactive-user scopes.
Review history reports need AccessReview.ReadWrite.All even to list, and only return definitions created in the last 30 days.
mapping: scope says what is reviewed (group members, app assignments, access package assignments, role assignments); instances hold each run, stages the multi-stage steps.

nodes.label: Access review decision
nodes.summary: One reviewer decision per principal and resource: approve or deny, the system recommendation, who decided, and whether it was applied.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID Governance (capabilities that were generally available in P2 still run on P2).
limits: Default page size is 100.
Insights (sign-in activity, membership outliers) come with $expand=insights.
mapping: principal is the user or service principal; resource is the group, app or role under review.
appliedBy and applyResult show whether a deny actually removed the access.

nodes.label: Access package
nodes.summary: A bundle of group memberships, app roles and SharePoint site roles that users request or are assigned, governed by policies for who can request, approval and expiry.

permissions.application: EntitlementManagement.Read.All (or give the app the Catalog reader role)

nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID Governance (capabilities that were generally available in P2 still run on P2). Custom extensions, auto-assignment policies, Verified ID and sponsor approvers need ID Governance.
limits: The list returns only packages the caller can read.
Catalog-scoped callers should use accessPackages?$expand=assignmentPolicies; listing all policies needs a directory role.
SharePoint site resources in a catalog are returned only with delegated permissions.
mapping: resourceRoleScopes say which group, app role or site role the package grants; catalog groups packages and resources.

nodes.label: Access package assignment
nodes.summary: Who holds which access package, under which policy and until when, plus the requests that created or removed it.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID Governance (capabilities that were generally available in P2 still run on P2).
limits: Catalog-scoped callers must filter by package: $filter=accessPackage/id eq '{id}'.
Both lists include expired assignments and past requests; filter on state eq 'Delivered' for current access.
mapping: $expand=target,accessPackage gives the user and package; target/objectId matches the user's object ID.

nodes.label: Connected organisation
nodes.summary: An external Entra tenant or domain whose users may request access packages, with internal and external sponsors.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID Governance (capabilities that were generally available in P2 still run on P2). Guests are billed by monthly active users and need a linked Azure subscription.
limits: Delegated callers need at least Identity Governance Administrator; catalog roles aren't enough.
state proposed means it was created automatically when a user from that tenant first requested access.
mapping: identitySources hold the tenant ID or domain; filter with identitySources/any(...).

nodes.label: Lifecycle workflow
nodes.summary: Joiner, mover and leaver automation: workflows triggered by employeeHireDate or employeeLeaveDateTime that run tasks such as disabling accounts or removing groups and access packages.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite.
limits: Runs and processing results need LifecycleWorkflows-Reports.Read.All.
Up to 100 workflows per tenant and 25 tasks per workflow (Learn's licensing page still says 50 workflows); offsetInDays from -180 to 180.
Setting employeeLeaveDateTime needs User-LifeCycleInfo.ReadWrite.All (plus User.Read.All).
mapping: The trigger reads employeeHireDate or employeeLeaveDateTime on the user; scope is a rule, optionally limited to administrative units.
runs and userProcessingResults are the evidence that a leaver's access was actually removed.

nodes.label: Terms of use
nodes.summary: Terms of use documents that a Conditional Access policy makes users accept, and the record of who accepted which version.
nodes.licence: Entra ID P1 or above.
limits: Delegated only, for agreements and for acceptances (AgreementAcceptance.Read).
Delegated callers need at least Security Reader.
mapping: A Conditional Access policy's grantControls.termsOfUse holds the agreement IDs; acceptances record userId and version.

nodes.label: PIM for groups
nodes.summary: Just-in-time membership or ownership of a group (often a role-assignable group): who is eligible to activate and who is active.
nodes.licence: Entra ID P2 or ID Governance. If the licence lapses, eligible assignments are removed and time-bound active ones become permanent.
limits: A $filter on groupId or principalId is required.
Active assignments are in assignmentSchedules (PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.Read.AzureADGroup); listing assignment requests needs the ReadWrite permission.
Admins who can manage groups (or AU-scoped admins) can change membership outside PIM through the groups API.
mapping: accessId is member or owner; group and principal are expandable.

nodes.label: Admin consent request
nodes.summary: Requests from users for admin consent to an app they couldn't consent to themselves, with each user's justification.
nodes.licence: Not stated on Learn (checked 16 Nov 2026).
limits: Requests only exist when the admin consent workflow is turned on (Global Administrator).
Filter pending requests with userConsentRequests/any(u:u/status eq 'InProgress').
mapping: appId identifies the app; approving creates an OAuth grant or app role assignment for it.
A reviewer's own queue: /users/{id}/appConsentRequestsForApproval (beta only).

nodes.label: Authentication method
nodes.summary: The sign-in methods a user has registered: FIDO2 keys and passkeys, Microsoft Authenticator, phone, Windows Hello for Business, Temporary Access Pass and others, one object per method.
limits: Microsoft advises against this API for audits across the whole user population; use the registration details report instead (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
Delegated calls on other users need Global Reader, Authentication Administrator or Privileged Authentication Administrator. An Authentication Administrator only sees masked phone numbers.
No OData query parameters are supported on the list.
lastUsedDateTime is best effort: null or missing doesn't mean the method was never used.
/me needs a delegated permission; application permissions aren't supported there.
mapping: Each method is typed by @odata.type, for example #microsoft.graph.fido2AuthenticationMethod; typed collections such as /authentication/fido2Methods exist too.

nodes.label: User registration details
nodes.summary: One row per user with MFA and self-service password reset registration and capability, passwordless capability, the methods registered and the system-preferred method. The way to measure MFA and passkey roll-out across a tenant.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 (authentication methods usage and insights) (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
limits: Doesn't return disabled users.
$filter works on isMfaCapable, isMfaRegistered, isSsprEnabled, isSsprRegistered, methodsRegistered, userDisplayName and userPrincipalName.
Delegated callers need Reports Reader, Security Reader, Security Administrator or Global Reader.
mapping: The id is the user's object ID, so rows join to /users/{id}.

nodes.label: Risk detection
nodes.summary: Each user risk event that Entra ID Protection detected, with its type (for example unfamiliar sign-in properties), level, state, IP address, location and the sign-in it came from.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, as stated on the List riskDetections page (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
limits: Default page size 20; $top up to 500.
Delegated callers need Global Reader, Security Operator, Security Reader or Security Administrator.
Not available in the China (21Vianet) cloud.
mapping: userId joins to /users/{id} and to the risky user; riskEventType says what was detected.

nodes.label: Risky service principal
nodes.summary: Apps and workload identities that Entra ID Protection flags as at risk, with risk level, state and history. The workload-identity counterpart of risky users.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
limits: Delegated callers need Global Reader, Security Operator, Security Reader or Security Administrator.
confirmCompromised and dismiss are bound actions; reading needs only the Read permission.
mapping: appId joins to the service principal's appId.

nodes.label: Cross-tenant access policy
nodes.summary: Which external tenants your users can collaborate with, and how: B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect in each direction, tenant restrictions, inbound trust (MFA and device claims) and automatic consent, as defaults and per partner.
limits: Delegated roles: Security Reader and Global Reader read basic properties; Global Secure Access Administrator and Teams Administrator read them without identity synchronisation settings; Security Administrator reads all.
Use $expand=identitySynchronization to list each partner's cross-tenant user sync policy.
mapping: Defaults live at /policies/crossTenantAccessPolicy/default; each partner is keyed by its tenantId.

nodes.label: Managed device (Intune)
nodes.summary: Devices enrolled in Intune: owner, OS, compliance state, encryption, last sync and management agent, plus remote actions such as retire and wipe.
nodes.licence: An active Intune licence for the tenant (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
limits: This is the Intune record, not the Entra device object: the two have different IDs.
Remote actions (retire, wipe and others) are bound POST actions on the device.
mapping: azureADDeviceId matches the Entra device's deviceId (not its object id).

nodes.label: Device compliance policy
nodes.summary: Intune compliance policies for every platform in one collection, with their assignments and per-device and per-user status. Device compliance feeds Conditional Access.
nodes.licence: An active Intune licence for the tenant (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
limits: The collection mixes platforms; tell them apart by @odata.type, for example #microsoft.graph.windows10CompliancePolicy.
Per-device results are under /deviceManagement/deviceCompliancePolicies/{id}/deviceStatuses.
mapping: A managed device's own view is /deviceManagement/managedDevices/{id}/deviceCompliancePolicyStates.

nodes.label: Attack simulation
nodes.summary: Phishing simulation campaigns from Attack simulation and training in Defender for Office 365: technique, status, launch and completion dates, payload and landing page.
nodes.licence: Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
limits: Global service only: not in the US Government or China (21Vianet) clouds.
$filter and $orderby work on attackTechnique, attackType, completionDateTime, displayName, isAutomated, launchDateTime and status.
mapping: User-level results: /reports/security/getAttackSimulationRepeatOffenders, getAttackSimulationSimulationUserCoverage and getAttackSimulationTrainingUserCoverage.

nodes.label: Secure Score control profile
nodes.summary: The catalogue of Secure Score improvement actions: title, category, maximum score, rank, implementation cost, user impact, threats, remediation and the tenant's control state updates.
limits: Profiles describe the controls; the scores themselves come from /security/secureScores.

nodes.label: Service health issue
nodes.summary: Current and recent incidents and advisories for the Microsoft 365 services your tenant subscribes to, with status, impact and updates; healthOverviews gives each service's current state.
limits: Delegated callers must hold at least one admin role (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
mapping: The incidentReport function on an issue returns the post-incident review.

nodes.label: Message centre post
nodes.summary: Message centre posts: upcoming changes, new features, retirements and planned maintenance for your tenant's services, with services, tags, action-required dates and attachments.
limits: Marking posts read, archived or favourite is per signed-in user and needs ServiceMessageViewpoint.Write (delegated only) (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
Delegated callers must hold at least one admin role.

nodes.label: Provisioning log
nodes.summary: Each create, update or delete that Entra provisioning made, from HR-driven inbound provisioning to outbound SaaS apps: source and target system and identity, steps, modified properties and status.
nodes.licence: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 (provisioning logs) (checked on Microsoft Learn, 28 Nov 2026).
limits: Supports $filter (eq, contains, gt, lt), $orderby, $top and $skiptoken; filters are case sensitive.
Delegated callers need a role such as Reports Reader, Security Reader, Global Reader or Application Administrator.
mapping: servicePrincipal.id joins to the provisioning app's service principal.

scenarios.label: Secure offboarding
scenarios.summary: A leaver's tokens, group access, app access, files and devices must all be cut off, not just the account disabled.
scenarios.licence: Entra ID (Free). Intune for device actions.

steps.do: Block sign-in (accountEnabled false), then revoke refresh tokens and session cookies.
steps.note: Revocation can take a few minutes, and access tokens already issued stay valid until they expire (usually about an hour).

steps.do: List memberOf and remove the user from groups, especially role-assignable and privileged ones.
steps.note: Dynamic group membership can't be removed by hand; it drops when the user's attributes change.

steps.do: Remove the user's direct enterprise app assignments.
steps.note: The list includes assignments through groups the user is a direct member of; remove those through the group.

steps.do: Find the OneDrive and hand its content to the manager before the retention period runs out.
steps.note: Setting the OneDrive access delegate (the manager) is a SharePoint admin setting, not a Graph call.

steps.do: Find the user's registered and owned devices and disable or retire them.
steps.note: Wipe and retire are Intune actions on managedDevice (/deviceManagement), not on the Entra device object.

seeAlsoNote.custodian-legal-hold: Do this first: put the leaver on hold before you block sign-in, remove licences or delete the OneDrive.
seeAlsoNote.leaver-event-retention: Fire the leaver event so their content is kept for the right period.

scenarios.label: Privileged access review
scenarios.summary: Standing admin roles are the biggest identity risk; a review should cover active and eligible assignments and how they are used.
scenarios.licence: Entra ID P2 or ID Governance for PIM. Entra ID P1 for sign-in logs.

steps.do: List active directory roles and their members.
steps.note: Only activated roles appear here. Use roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments for the full picture.

steps.do: List eligible assignments: who can activate which role, and when that ends.
Check each holder: still employed, a cloud-only admin account, MFA registered.
Check roles scoped to administrative units, which a tenant-wide review misses.
Look for admin sign-ins without MFA or from unusual places.

scenarios.label: Risky app consent review
scenarios.summary: Consent phishing and over-permissioned apps give attackers durable access that survives password resets.
scenarios.licence: Entra ID (Free). Entra ID P1 for sign-in logs.

steps.do: List apps registered in your tenant and their requested permissions (requiredResourceAccess).
List enterprise apps, including multi-tenant apps from other publishers.
Find delegated grants with broad scopes (Mail.Read, Files.Read.All and so on), and whether they are admin or per-user consent.
Find application permissions granted to each app: these work without a signed-in user.
steps.note: Application permissions on Microsoft Graph are app role assignments whose resourceId is the Graph service principal.

steps.do: Check whether the app is actually used, and from where.
steps.note: Service principal sign-ins are beta only; v1.0 returns interactive user sign-ins.

scenarios.label: Guest and external access review
scenarios.summary: Guests and shared channels quietly widen who can see your content; access should be reviewed where it is granted.
scenarios.licence: Entra ID (Free). Access reviews need ID Governance or P2.

steps.do: List guest accounts and when they last signed in.
Find which groups and Microsoft 365 groups each guest belongs to.
List the teams behind those groups and their guest settings.
Find shared channels, whose members can come from other tenants without a guest account.
steps.note: Shared-channel members from other tenants are not guests, so a guest review misses them.

steps.do: Find the sites behind those teams and channels (shared channels have their own site).
List sharing links and direct grants, especially anyone and external links.

scenarios.label: Compromised account investigation
scenarios.summary: Business email compromise moves fast; you need the alert, the sign-ins, the persistence (rules) and the containment in one sweep.
scenarios.licence: Microsoft Defender XDR. Entra ID P2 for risky users. Entra ID P1 for sign-in logs.

steps.do: Open the Defender XDR incident and its correlated alerts.
Read the alert evidence: user, mailbox, IP addresses, files.
Check the user's risk level and history; confirm compromise to feed ID Protection.
Review sign-ins for the period: locations, apps, MFA results, legacy protocols.
Look for changes the attacker made: MFA methods added, app consents, role changes.
Look for Inbox rules that forward, redirect, delete or hide mail.
Hunt across mail, identity and cloud app events for the same IP addresses and patterns.
steps.note: Advanced hunting keeps 30 days of data.

steps.do: Contain: block sign-in, reset the password and revoke sessions.

scenarios.label: Dormant accounts with active licences
scenarios.summary: Unused accounts are an attack surface and a cost; licences on them are money spent for nothing.

steps.do: List users with their last successful sign-in and assigned licences.
steps.note: signInActivity can lag by up to 24 hours, and lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime has no data before December 2023.

steps.do: Confirm inactivity for borderline accounts; non-interactive sign-ins (beta) show background use.
steps.note: Sign-in logs are kept for 30 days, so use signInActivity for anything older.

steps.do: Map skuId to product names and see consumed against purchased units.
Find group-based licence assignments; remove the user from the group rather than the licence.
steps.note: Needs ConsistencyLevel: eventual. Licence errors are written to the user asynchronously.

steps.do: Confirm per-workload inactivity (mail, OneDrive, Teams) from the activity reports.
steps.note: Reports show concealed names unless the tenant setting is turned off.

scenarios.label: Mail forwarding to external addresses
scenarios.summary: Auto-forwarding is a classic exfiltration route, and it can be set in places Graph can't see.
scenarios.licence: Exchange Online. Defender XDR for alerts and hunting.

steps.do: List mailbox users in scope.
For each mailbox, find Inbox rules with forwardTo, redirectTo or forwardAsAttachmentTo outside your domains.
steps.note: Reading every mailbox's rules app-only needs MailboxSettings.Read for the whole tenant; scope it with RBAC for Applications if you can.

steps.do: Check mailbox forwarding, the outbound spam policy, remote domains and transport rules in Exchange Online PowerShell.
steps.permission: Exchange Online PowerShell role (for example View-Only Organization Management)

steps.do: Look for forwarding alerts, such as suspicious email forwarding activity.
Hunt for mail actually leaving to external recipients.

scenarios.label: Oversharing check before Copilot rollout
scenarios.summary: Copilot surfaces whatever a user can already open, so overshared sites become Copilot answers.
scenarios.licence: Microsoft 365 Copilot. SharePoint Advanced Management for its oversharing reports.

steps.do: List sites and spot broadly shared ones (Everyone except external users, large Members groups).
steps.note: getAllSites needs application permissions.

steps.do: List site and file permissions and sharing links, especially organisation-wide and anyone links.
Find sensitive files in those sites (search or by library) and their labels.
Check which labels exist and apply or raise labels on sensitive content.
steps.note: assignSensitivityLabel is a metered API, and app-only calls can't replace the content of a labelled file.

steps.do: Track Copilot readiness and usage after rollout.
steps.note: Check Learn for the current Copilot usage report endpoints; some are beta.

scenarios.label: Apply Purview DLP to your own AI apps
scenarios.summary: Home-grown AI apps can leak data like any other; the Purview APIs let them honour the same DLP and labels as Microsoft 365.
scenarios.licence: Pay-as-you-go billing for Entra-registered AI apps. Purview DLP licensing for the policies.

steps.do: Identify the user the app acts for (delegated) or will act for (application).
Compute protection scopes, then send each prompt and response to processContent and honour the verdict.
steps.note: Cache the compute ETag and send it as If-None-Match; call compute again when protectionScopeState is modified.

steps.do: Read the labels that apply to the content the app retrieves, so it can respect encryption and usage rights.
DLP matches from your app surface as alerts for the security team.

scenarios.label: Copilot interaction export and review
scenarios.summary: Prompts and responses are business records; you may need to export, review, retain or hold them.
scenarios.licence: Microsoft 365 Copilot. Purview (eDiscovery Premium) for review sets and holds.

steps.do: Pick the users in scope; only Copilot-licensed users have history.
Export prompts and responses for a date range, filtered by app if needed.
Follow contexts and attachments to the files Copilot used.
Or to the mails and chats it used.
Keep the interactions under a retention policy for Copilot interactions.
steps.note: Copilot retention is set by retention policy in Purview, not by labelling each interaction through Graph.

steps.do: Or put the users on hold and collect Copilot interactions into a case.

scenarios.label: Audit and hunt AI usage
scenarios.summary: Security teams need to see who uses AI, on what data, and spot misuse such as prompt-based exfiltration.
scenarios.licence: Purview Audit (Standard). Defender XDR (with Defender for Cloud Apps) for CloudAppEvents.

steps.do: Search the unified audit log for CopilotInteraction records.
steps.note: Audit queries run asynchronously; poll the query status, then read its records.

steps.do: Hunt in CloudAppEvents for AI app activity across users.
Pivot to the users with unusual volume or access patterns.
Check for related alerts, such as DLP or insider risk on AI activity.

scenarios.label: Agent identity governance
scenarios.summary: AI agents now have their own identities; they need an owner, least privilege, Conditional Access and monitoring like any workforce identity.
scenarios.licence: Microsoft Agent 365 (in Microsoft 365 E7) plus Entra ID P1 for Conditional Access on agents. Drifting; checked 16 Nov 2026.

steps.do: Inventory blueprints and their owners and sponsors.
List agent identities and the blueprint each came from.
Check that a Conditional Access policy targets agent identities or their blueprints.
steps.note: Policies for all users don't include agent users; agents need explicit targeting (preview).

steps.do: Review delegated and application permissions granted to agents.
Monitor agent sign-ins.
steps.call: GET /beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'
steps.note: The agent property on sign-ins is beta only.

scenarios.label: Event-based retention for leavers
scenarios.summary: A leaver's records must be kept for a set time from the day they leave, not from when each file was created.
scenarios.licence: Event-based retention and disposition review: Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E5/A5/G5, Purview Suite, or E5 Information Protection and Governance (Purview service description, checked 16 Nov 2026).

steps.do: Get the leaver's employee ID; it is the asset ID that tags their content.
steps.note: Content must carry the asset ID (the Compliance Asset Id column) before the event fires, or it won't be matched.

steps.do: Use a label whose retention starts on an event (retentionTrigger dateOfEvent), bound to an Employee leaving event type.
steps.note: Delegated only. The event type can't be changed once the label is saved.

steps.do: Create a retention event of that type with an asset ID query, for example AssetID:<employee ID>.
steps.note: eventQueries match SharePoint and OneDrive by asset ID and Exchange by keywords.

steps.do: Check the event-based label is applied to the leaver's files.
At the end of the period, reviewers approve deletion in the Purview portal.
steps.note: Reviewers need the Disposition Management role; auditing must be on.

scenarios.label: Legal hold on a departing custodian
scenarios.summary: If a leaver may be part of litigation, their mailbox and files must be preserved before anything is removed.
scenarios.licence: Microsoft 365 E3 for cases, custodians, searches and holds with delegated calls. E5 or an equivalent eDiscovery add-on for review sets and app-only calls.

steps.do: Open or create the case.
steps.note: Delegated callers also need the eDiscovery Manager or eDiscovery Administrator role.

steps.do: Add the leaver as a custodian with their mailbox and OneDrive, plus the sites and groups they used.
Put the custodian on hold before sign-in is blocked, licences are removed or the OneDrive is deleted.
steps.note: applyHold is v1.0 and asynchronous; the legalHolds list is beta only in $metadata.

steps.do: Search the custodian's sources and estimate the volume.
Collect the results into a review set and export them.
steps.note: On E3 there are no review sets, and export needs pay-as-you-go billing.

scenarios.label: DLP incident triage
scenarios.summary: A DLP alert is only the start; triage needs the matching activity, the content, its label and what was detected.
scenarios.licence: DLP alert investigation: Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E5/A5, E5 Compliance, or E5 Information Protection and Governance. Audit (Standard) covers 180 days.

steps.do: List DLP alerts and pick one to triage.
steps.note: Single-event DLP alerts work on any DLP subscription; aggregated alerts need E5-class licences.

steps.do: Query the audit log for DLP rule matches around the alert time.
Read the records: who, which file or message, which rule and what action was taken.
For SharePoint and OneDrive matches, open the file and who it is shared with.
For Exchange matches, find the email.
And trace where the email went.
steps.call: GET /admin/exchange/tracing/messageTraces?$filter=receivedDateTime ge {start} and receivedDateTime le {end} and senderAddress eq '{address}'

steps.do: Check the content's label and whether it was downgraded or removed.
Identify which sensitive info types matched.
steps.note: The matched SITs are in the DLP audit record; the sensitiveTypes list itself is beta and undocumented.
